summary: Replace ShipRight's hand-built sign-in (own JWT, refresh tokens, password reset, Company/User tables, IsAdmin flag) with ASP.NET Core Identity backed by the existing Dapper-style data access (no EF Core), add roles, Google sign-in, and per-company (tenant, CompanyId) scoping of users, logins and roles. Decided: existing accounts and passwords keep working. Still open: which roles exist, how Google sign-in joins a company, how a company is identified at login, and same-email-in-two-companies.

ask.text: Today every account is either an admin or not (the first person who signs up for a company is the admin). Which roles should people be able to have inside a company?
ask.why: It decides which roles are created, who may do what in the app, and what the role-protected endpoints and tests check.

options.label: Two roles: Admin and Member
options.consequence: Matches today's admin/non-admin split. Existing admins become Admin, everyone else Member. Admin manages the company's users and roles.

options.label: Three roles: Admin, Operator and Viewer
options.consequence: Operators can build and deploy, Viewers can only look. More rules to define and test across every existing screen.

options.label: Admin-defined roles
options.consequence: Admins create their own roles per company. Most flexible, but needs screens to manage roles and a permission model.
